issues.legal_issue: A registrar cannot use a record-correction application to reverse a finding made in a public-trust registration proceeding when the governing statutory scheme makes that finding final and provides a separate civil-suit remedy to challenge it.
material_facts: The Registrar registered the trust and recorded the temple and its shops as trust property after an application for registration was considered.
A separate registration application concerning the temple was later withdrawn without a final finding in that proceeding.
The Registrar subsequently allowed an application to correct the record and recorded the temple as a private trust.
The statutory scheme provided a civil suit to challenge a finding made in the registration inquiry.
issues.conclusion: The original registration finding became final and conclusive, and the Registrar had no authority to reverse it through a correction application; the finding could be challenged only through the prescribed civil suit.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4, 5, 6 and 7 of the M.P. Public Trusts Act, 1951 provide for an inquiry, findings and entries in the register, with the entries final and conclusive subject to the Act. Section 8 provides the remedy of a civil suit to set aside or modify a finding. Because the separate application had been withdrawn without a final finding, its inquiry report could not establish that the registration finding in the other proceeding resulted from a clerical mistake.

rule.if: public_trust_registration_case and registrar_recorded_finding_after_inquiry and finding_entered_in_public_register and later_record_correction_changed_finding and civil_suit_remedy_available

predicates.public_trust_registration_case: The proceeding concerned whether a trust was a public trust and whether property belonged to it.
predicates.registrar_recorded_finding_after_inquiry: The registrar made a finding after conducting an inquiry into the registration application.
predicates.finding_entered_in_public_register: The registrar entered the finding in the public register.
predicates.later_record_correction_changed_finding: The registrar later changed the registered finding through a record-correction process.
predicates.civil_suit_remedy_available: A separate civil action was available to challenge or modify the registration finding.

issues.definition: When a registrar has entered an inquiry finding in the public register and a civil action is available to challenge it, a later record correction cannot reverse that finding.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot use a writ petition to challenge an order after pursuing and losing the statutory appeal against that same order in the same High Court.
material_facts: The District Judge made an order on a statutory reference, and the Act treated that order as a decree appealable to the High Court.
The affected party appealed to the High Court, but the appeal was dismissed.
The party later filed a writ petition challenging the same order, and the High Court allowed it.
issues.conclusion: The writ petition was not maintainable, and the High Court erred in entertaining and allowing it after the statutory appeal had been pursued and dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 27(3) of the M.P. Public Trusts Act, 1951 treated the court’s order as a decree and provided an appeal to the High Court. The Court relied on Shankar Ramchandra Abhyankar v. Krishnaji Dattatreya Bapat, which held that, where a party has chosen and exhausted one mode of invoking the High Court’s jurisdiction, granting relief through another proceeding against the same order is not a proper exercise of discretion and may undermine finality and prevent abuse of process. The Court also noted that exceptional circumstances, such as lack of jurisdiction or violation of fundamental rights or natural justice, can justify writ relief despite an alternative remedy, but the statutory appeal here had already been used and dismissed.

rule.if: appeal_from_statutory_court_order_case and statutory_appeal_to_same_high_court_available and party_pursued_that_appeal and appeal_dismissed and later_writ_challenged_same_order

predicates.appeal_from_statutory_court_order_case: The proceeding was an appeal concerning a court order made under a statutory process.
predicates.statutory_appeal_to_same_high_court_avai: The law provided an appeal against the order to the same High Court later asked to hear the writ petition.
predicates.party_pursued_that_appeal: The party challenging the order filed the statutory appeal.
predicates.appeal_dismissed: The High Court dismissed the statutory appeal.
predicates.later_writ_challenged_same_order: The party later filed a writ petition challenging the same order.

issues.definition: When a party pursues and loses a statutory appeal to a High Court, the party cannot later use a writ petition in that High Court to challenge the same order.

issues.legal_issue: A party may be given a fresh opportunity to bring the prescribed civil suit when an earlier record correction left the party with no occasion to file it.
material_facts: The Registrar had recorded the temple as a private trust through a correction order.
In light of that record, the affected party had no occasion to file a civil suit to establish its position.
The Supreme Court set aside the High Court judgments and considered it just to permit a civil suit.
issues.conclusion: The contesting respondents were permitted to institute a civil suit within three months from the judgment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8 of the M.P. Public Trusts Act, 1951 provides a civil suit to challenge or modify a registration finding. In view of the peculiar circumstances, including that the Registrar’s correction order meant there had been no occasion to file that suit, the Court granted an opportunity to pursue the remedy in the interest of justice.

predicates.appeal_against_writ_judgment_case: The proceeding was an appeal challenging a judgment that had allowed a writ petition.
predicates.registrar_recorded_private_trust_by_corr: The registrar used a correction process to record the property as a private trust.
predicates.affected_party_had_no_occasion_to_file_c: The affected party had no occasion to bring the civil suit because of the registrar’s correction order.
predicates.court_considers_fresh_opportunity_just: The court considered a fresh opportunity to bring the civil suit just in the circumstances.

issues.definition: When a correction order left an affected party with no occasion to bring a civil suit and the court considers a fresh opportunity just, the party may institute the suit.
